Reproduction steps:
1. Open `node_3d_vs_shader.tres` visual shader resource
2. Open inside the visual shader the group node by clicking on the Edit icon
3. On the Group input node inside the group node click on `Edit ports`
4. Click repeatedly on `Remove port` (trashbin icon)
My bug is solved now and all looks solid from my side.

Did a review of the code and found some problems.

The discoverability and usability of the feature is rather poor right now, but since improving it is already in the plans, I won't comment on it.

I noticed that Group Input/Output nodes can be removed from the group (with Delete). The editor does not support it properly, so it should be blocked I think.

Tested locally, it works as expected. Example with a group that brightens a color with an orange tint: I've tested the output in normal + headless PCK export (with `.godot/` removed before each export) and both work correctly. Nested groups work, although I was able to get a shader compilation error once (I unfortunately can't reproduce it): ``` --res://new_shader.tres-- 26 | 27 | E 28-> group_Node_group_734b3b5c(, n_out1p0); 29 | 30 | SHADER ERROR: Expected expression, found: 'COMMA'. at: (null) (res://new_shader.tres:28) ERROR: Shader compilation failed. at: (servers\rendering\renderer_rd\forward_clustered\scene_shader_forward_clustered.cpp:185) ``` In terms of UX, I actually found this fairly intuitive to use, although "group" isn't the most obvious name for creating functions when you're used to text shaders. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/88981 could help with this by adding `[Function]` as a shortcut notation, so that it'll appear when entering "function" in the node search. Some feedback: - The default name "Node group" should be "NodeGroup", as we use title case with no spaces for node names: - Clicking the edit button has no effect if there is no VisualShaderGroup resource assigned. I suggest either hiding the button in this case, or making it automatically create a new VisualShaderGroup resource (then edit this new group) when clicked. - More generally, we could probably automatically create a new VisualShaderGroup resource each time you create a VisualShaderGroupNode in the visual shader editor. This would follow the workflow established by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/88647 (and which was already present in nodes like Curve2D with `PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR_INSTANTIATE_OBJECT` beforehand). - That said, one of the behaviors mentioned above should still be implemented in case you clear the default VisualShaderGroup resource. - As an aside, I noticed the `` text doesn't fit in full. This isn't the only location in the editor where it's an issue: Maybe switching the placeholder to `(empty)` will reduce the number of these occurrences. - The margin at the bottom of the node should be increased slightly (or a margin should be added to the error message), so that the error message doesn't appear too close to the bottom of the node. Compare with the output node on the right: - "Edit ports" button should be "Edit Ports": The same applies to the dialog titles, which should also use Title Case: - Opening the Edit Group Ports dialog on the input/output when there are no parameters yet should automatically create one parameter, as you'll always need at least one. This saves a click. - When adding a new parameter in the Edit Group Ports dialog, it should use type of the currently specified parameter. This makes it faster to add several parameters that aren't of the Float type (adding several Vector3/Vector4 in a row is common). - Exiting a group could be made more obvious somehow, perhaps by adding a tinted background behind the "exit" button, similar to node-specific menus in the 3D editor: The highlight should be less strong than a pressed button (i.e. less strong than the Toggle Shader Preview button besides it on the above screenshot). For future PRs: - It could be possible to drag-and-drop a VisualShaderGroup resource to the visual shader to create a VisualShaderGroupNode with the group automatically assigned.

Looks good enough now.
I noticed some of my comments were marked as resolved, without being resolved .-.
